newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch down at slow start, await Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch down at slow start, await Dow.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened marginally down on Tuesday on what traders said was cautious dealing while the market awaited developments on Wall Street.
"We're totally dependent on the New York Stock Exchange. Several ADRs are off, so dealers here are cautious and waiting to see which way the Dow turns," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was off 1.94 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.05 percent, at 3,928.15.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was meanwhile down 14.42 points at 7,278.33.
Trading volume .TV.MX was a sign of caution at 3.7 million shares.
"Still, it opened that way yesterday and, like yesterday, it could soon pick up if the Dow rallies," the trader added.
Financial stock Bancomer weighed most on the market, accounting for 40 percent of shares traded in early dealing, and was off two centavos to 2.85 pesos.
"It's nothing fundamental. The stock is volatile and more than half of its volume was on cross-trades," a desk trader said.

Telmex also weighed heavily on the downside, and was down eight centavos at 17.26 pesos, after reaching a record close in peso terms on Monday. Dealers said the telecom had moved parallel to its ADRs, off 1/2 at 43-1/4.
Dealers said there was no clear downward trend among blue chips, however.
"The market is selective. Many blue chips are flat and some, like Alfa and Cemex, are in demand as they are still cheap," a floor trader said.
Conglomerate Alfa was up 40 centavos to 47.80 pesos, while cement maker Cemex was ahead 10 centavos at 28.90 pesos.

Dealers said media group Televisa, off 1.30 at 97.70 pesos, was hurt by an announcement late Monday of a management reshuffle. The stock has been volatile since the unexpected retirement and sudden death on April 16 of its long-serving chairman, Emilio Azcrraga Milmo.
Televisa ADRs were meanwhile off 1/4 to 24-5/8.
